scientific_question: Can MemoryOS and MemGAS be exposed through source-authoritative, project-owned execution copies without modifying their accepted official checkouts?
decision_informed: Whether the two methods can proceed to isolated dependency and lifecycle gates.
scientific_evidence_role: engineering source-copy and adapter-code gate only; no lifecycle or numerical claim is permitted

methods.copy_scope: tracked files beneath memoryos-pypi only, renamed to the importable package memoryos_pkg
all tracked files except every __pycache__ component and .pyc file

execution_contract.wave1_non_interference: The copy stage may run while Wave-1 is active because it performs no model download, dependency installation, model load, API call, or GPU operation.

acceptance: The source checkout resolves to the exact method revision and is clean.
Only Git-tracked regular files are copied.
The destination and evidence roots were absent before execution.
No copied relative path contains __pycache__ and no copied file ends in .pyc.
Every copied file has a retained relative path, byte size, and SHA-256.
The evidence root has TERMINAL_ACCEPTED, no TERMINAL_REJECTED, and a verified evidence inventory.
failure: Any collision, source identity mismatch, dirty source, non-regular tracked file, copy error, bytecode inclusion, or timeout seals a fresh TERMINAL_REJECTED evidence root and retains the partial destination.
next_gate_after_acceptance: Independently audit both execution copies and overlay hashes, then freeze isolated dependency environments. No model or lifecycle execution is authorized by this stage.
prohibited_actions: editing either accepted official source checkout
copying untracked files or tracked bytecode into the execution source
installing dependencies, downloading models, calling an LLM, or using a GPU
starting a lifecycle or numerical run
deleting or repairing a rejected destination in place
